title: Хронический отит и подозрение на среднее ухо
terminology: Chronic otitis externa, otitis media and otitis interna are related but separate disease levels.
A normal-looking, intact or unvisualized tympanic membrane does not exclude otitis media.
Canal stenosis, exudate, anatomy, pain and patient limits are recorded as unknown visibility rather than intact tympanum.
External-canal cytology or culture is not middle-ear truth; a decision-changing middle-ear question requires a true middle-ear sample.
CT or MRI supports bulla, bone, canal and inner-ear assessment, but incidental bulla fluid requires clinical correlation.
Otitis media can cause pain, facial nerve, Horner, dry-eye and hearing signs; neurologic head tilt indicates inner-ear or another vestibular route rather than media alone.
A peripheral vestibular pattern remains a localization, not automatic proof of otitis interna.
Both ears are assessed and laterality, tympanic integrity, sample level and prior procedures persist longitudinally.
Feline inflammatory polyp, primary secretory disease, infection and mass remain separate authored branches.
Mass-like disease requires tissue diagnosis; cholesteatoma is not automatically neoplasia.
Painful stenotic ears are not repeatedly forced awake.
No drug, dose, topical-safety decision, cleaning solution, myringotomy, flush or surgery technique is generated.

commonHistoryQuestions.prompt: Сколько эпизодов, какое ухо и как долго держался ответ?
Какие исследования и процедуры были, с какой стороны и на каком уровне?
Больно ли открывать рот, жевать или трогать голову/шею?
Есть ли наклон головы, падение, нистагм или асимметрия морды?
Есть ли сухость глаза, изменение зрачка или третьего века?
Изменился ли слух и как это проверяли?
Чем и как чистили ухо и была ли целостность перепонки известна?
Есть ли skin, allergy или endocrine pattern?
У кошки есть nasal noise, dysphagia или polyp/procedure history?
Были ли foreign body, травма, агрессивная чистка или процедура перед ухудшением?
Есть ли fever, снижение аппетита или изменение mentation?
Какие referral, cost, transport и handling ограничения реальны?

outcomes.safe: Recurrence is connected to middle-ear and primary-cause evidence.
outcomes.unsafe: The same blind treatment is repeated indefinitely.

examFindings.finding: Status explicitly remains unknown.
Awake examination stops before injury or unreliable inference.

followUp.timing: after safe visualization/imaging and pain-aware intervention

outcomes.unsafe: Pain is overridden and an unseen membrane is called intact.

presentations.complaint: Recurrent bacterial or mixed cytology persists after prior exposure, raising resistance, biofilm, depth and cause questions.

historyAnswers.prior_cytology_culture_video_ct_mri_surg: Organisms, sites, susceptibility and exposure history dated.

variants.title: Средний отит при интактной или недоступной осмотру барабанной перепонке
variants.diagnosticTruth: Otitis media remains possible with a normal-looking, intact or unvisualized tympanic membrane; clinical suspicion, video assessment, bilateral advanced imaging and true middle-ear sampling have complementary roles, and incidental bulla material requires correlation.

presentations.complaint: The membrane appears normal, but recurrence, oral-opening pain, cranial-nerve signs or imaging supports a middle-ear question.

historyAnswers.mouth_opening_chewing_head_neck_pain: Middle-ear pain present or authored absent.

examFindings.finding: Appearance is one finding, not a rule-out.
Evidence levels remain separate.

investigations.result: Normal-looking or intact membrane recorded without exclusion claim.

followUp.timing: after depth confirmation and by tympanum/neuro/hearing response

outcomes.safe: A normal view is correctly integrated rather than used as a false exclusion.
outcomes.unsafe: The visible membrane closes a supported middle-ear differential.

ownerCommunication: Explain that the membrane is a boundary view, not a full picture of the bulla.

presentations.complaint: The tympanic membrane is bulging, opaque, thickened or discolored, requiring correlation and a middle-ear route.

examFindings.finding: Air, fluid, tissue and inflammation remain discriminators.
No code-generated myringotomy or flush.

outcomes.safe: Abnormal appearance triggers correlated evidence and safe procedure planning.
outcomes.unsafe: Bulging alone is called bacterial infection or prompts an improvised procedure.

ownerCommunication: Explain what the abnormal membrane suggests and why it does not identify the material behind it.

presentations.complaint: One symptomatic ear leads to evidence of bilateral or subclinical contralateral middle-ear disease.

examFindings.finding: Opposite ear is not ignored because it is quiet.
Clinical and sample evidence stays side-specific.

followUp.timing: side-specific response and bilateral imaging/tympanum checkpoint

outcomes.safe: Both ears remain separate longitudinal objects with correlated evidence.
outcomes.unsafe: The quiet ear is ignored or both sides inherit one culture result.

ownerCommunication: Explain why both ears are checked but may not share the same cause or sample result.

variants.title: Средний отит с разрывом барабанной перепонки
variants.diagnosticTruth: A ruptured tympanic membrane changes the safety and anatomic route: spontaneous, foreign-body, traumatic or iatrogenic modifiers persist, external and true middle-ear samples remain distinct, and procedures or topical-safety choices require reviewed specialist evidence.

presentations.complaint: Otorrhea and a documented spontaneous tympanic rupture indicate a middle-ear route rather than routine externa.

examFindings.finding: Tympanic integrity and laterality explicit.
Safety decision transferred to reviewed clinician/procedure.

followUp.timing: post-procedure/medical review with tympanum, cytology, neuro and hearing checkpoints

outcomes.safe: Rupture is managed as middle-ear disease with explicit safety boundaries.
outcomes.unsafe: Routine blind cleaning or generated topical advice continues.

ownerCommunication: Explain that the open membrane changes which procedures and products are safe to consider.

presentations.complaint: A foreign body, trauma, aggressive cleaning or procedure precedes tympanic rupture and acute deterioration.

historyAnswers.cleaning_products_technique_and_known_ty: Exact exposure context recorded without declaring toxicity.

examFindings.finding: Event is not erased by later infection.
Inner-ear/nerve injury route opened.

followUp.timing: urgent anatomic/neuro reassessment then tympanic and hearing recovery

outcomes.safe: The precipitating event and complications remain linked in one episode.
outcomes.unsafe: The event is erased or an improvised removal/flush is generated.

ownerCommunication: Describe the suspected link without assigning blame and state the urgent safety questions.

presentations.complaint: A true middle-ear sample differs from external-canal cytology or culture in the same ear.

historyAnswers.prior_cytology_culture_video_ct_mri_surg: Both samples retain date, side and anatomic level.
historyAnswers.episodes_laterality_response_timeline: Response is tied to the correct level.

examFindings.finding: Each result keeps side and level.

variants.title: Внутренний отит и периферический вестибулярный синдром
variants.diagnosticTruth: A peripheral vestibular pattern with compatible ear/middle-ear evidence can support otitis interna, but localization is not etiology; mentation, proprioception, nystagmus pattern, cranial nerves, ocular safety, hearing and central differentials determine urgency and imaging route.

presentations.complaint: Head tilt, horizontal or rotary nystagmus and vestibular ataxia occur with compatible ear disease.

historyAnswers.hearing_change_and_test_confidence: Hearing change and evidence confidence recorded.

examFindings.finding: Etiology requires correlated depth evidence.
Falling patient is protected and referred.

followUp.timing: continuous mobility/mentation then neuro, hearing and ear response

outcomes.safe: Peripheral localization and ear evidence are correlated with safe support.
outcomes.unsafe: Any head tilt is automatically called inner-ear infection.

ownerCommunication: Explain that the balance pattern localizes the problem but imaging/evidence must identify the cause.

presentations.complaint: Facial weakness, Horner signs, reduced tear production, ocular exposure or hearing deficit accompanies middle/inner-ear disease.

examFindings.finding: Exposure injury risk recorded.
Objective referral route available.

followUp.timing: immediate ocular checkpoint then serial cranial nerve/hearing recovery

outcomes.safe: Ocular safety and objective deficit monitoring accompany ear treatment.
outcomes.unsafe: The eye is ignored or hearing prognosis is declared from behavior alone.

ownerCommunication: Explain which nerve signs require eye protection and why hearing recovery may remain uncertain.

presentations.complaint: Severe vestibular signs include altered mentation, proprioceptive deficits, vertical/discordant nystagmus or other central red flags despite ear history.

historyAnswers.episodes_laterality_response_timeline: Ear history retained but not anchoring.

examFindings.finding: Central localization remains visible.

followUp.timing: continuous neurologic safety through specialist handoff

outcomes.safe: Central disease remains active and urgent despite a plausible ear history.
outcomes.unsafe: Every severe vestibular case is forced into otitis interna.

ownerCommunication: State that some findings do not fit a simple inner-ear localization and require urgent neurologic imaging.

outcomes.unsafe: The visible fragment is treated as the entire disease.

ownerCommunication: Explain that a polyp may extend between the bulla, ear and nasopharynx and requires mapping.

presentations.complaint: Bulla fluid or compatible middle-ear signs occur without sufficient evidence to assume routine bacterial infection.

historyAnswers.systemic_fever_appetite_mentation: Systemic infection evidence present or absent as authored.

outcomes.unsafe: Every bulla opacity becomes bacterial otitis media.

variants.title: Терминальный ушной канал, холестеатома или объёмное образование

presentations.complaint: The canal is mineralized, stenotic or obliterated with chronic pain and poor quality of life despite prior medical attempts.

historyAnswers.episodes_laterality_response_timeline: Long same-ear progression and response fixed.

examFindings.finding: Medical repetition no longer assumed curative.
Surgical referral is not automatic from appearance alone.

followUp.timing: pain/QOL checkpoint through imaging, decision and post-referral outcome

outcomes.safe: Irreversibility and QOL trigger informed salvage assessment with reversible factors retained.
outcomes.unsafe: Blind medical cycles continue or surgery is offered without extent review.

ownerCommunication: Explain why the anatomy may no longer permit durable medical control and what the referral must assess.

presentations.complaint: Progressive bulla expansion, keratinous material or bone change raises cholesteatoma and other destructive-disease differentials.

examFindings.finding: Cancer label requires separate tissue evidence.

outcomes.unsafe: Cholesteatoma is called cancer or managed as routine debris.

examFindings.finding: Inflammatory, polypoid, keratinous and neoplastic branches remain.

outcomes.unsafe: Appearance alone assigns cancer or triggers an instant operation.

familyValidationRules: Reject if normal, intact or unvisualized tympanum excludes otitis media.
Reject if external-canal culture becomes middle-ear culture or bulla fluid automatically means infection.
Reject if every head tilt becomes otitis interna or central neurologic red flags are hidden.
Reject if a painful stenotic ear is repeatedly forced awake or the opposite ear is ignored.
Reject if recurrent polyp becomes a new patient, mass automatically becomes neoplasia or cholesteatoma becomes cancer.
Reject if imaging or procedures are instant or code generates a drug, dose, topical-safety decision, cleaning solution, myringotomy, flush or surgery technique.
